    The hyperlinear-radical reduction lemma #

    This is the convergent target of the operator-algebraic ¬CEP program: six independent routes reduce "a finite game algebra with a trace but no amenable (matrix-microstate) trace" to a single statement about an LCS solution group Γ with central involution J.

    For B = C*(Γ)/(u_J + 1) (forcing J ↦ -1):

    (no amenable trace on B) ⟺ J ∈ Rad_hyp(Γ).

    The mathematical proof (both directions) is complete (the ⇐ direction is a fixed 2-norm-gap contradiction; ⇒ is the central-corner / corner-stability argument). This file lands the statement against the framework's Lean substrate and closes the ⇐ direction modulo one isolated mechanical fact (L2Seminorm of the constant -2).

    Substrate reused: TracialState, IsAmenableTrace, L2Seminorm (...CEP.Basic), GroupCStarRepresentation (...CEP.IRSDictionary).

    The residual field-hard content does NOT live here: it is the EXISTENCE of an LCS solution group with J ≠ 1 and J ∈ Rad_hyp(Γ) (equivalently the Taller–Vidick ε=0 / non-hyperlinear-group problem). This file isolates that the GAP reduces to that one existence statement.

      source
      def ZFib.CEP.InHyperlinearRadical (Γ : Type u) [Group Γ] (g : Γ) :
      Prop

      The hyperlinear radical, trace-level form (atk-a definition): g lies in the radical iff, in every group C*-representation carrying an amenable trace, g is sent to 1 in the trace 2-seminorm. The universal quantifier over amenable traces (not an existential over microstates) is essential — the trivial representation would otherwise place every element in the radical.

        theorem ZFib.CEP.L2Seminorm_neg_two {B : Type u} [CStarAlgebra B] [PartialOrder B] [StarOrderedRing B] (τ : TracialState B) :
        L2Seminorm τ (-1 - 1) = 2

        Isolated mechanical fact: the trace 2-seminorm of the constant -2 = (-1) - 1 is 2 (hence nonzero). L2Seminorm τ x = sqrt (Re (τ (star x * x))); here star (-2) * (-2) = 4·1, τ (4·1) = 4, sqrt 4 = 2. Pure scalar/PositiveLinearMap algebra; isolated so the reduction lemma below closes modulo exactly this.

        ¬HasAmenableTrace B

        ⇐ direction of the reduction (atk-a, fixed 2-norm-gap contradiction): if J is in the hyperlinear radical and ρ is a representation sending J ↦ -1 (the quotient condition), then B carries no amenable trace. Closes modulo L2Seminorm_neg_two.
